entry.title: New page: Jev browser use and computer use (TypeSafe AI). Of 7 Jev browser and computer-use agents read in source, none clicks or types when Jev errors, but 5 act on low-confidence answers, and only 1 asks a person before send, buy or delete.

New page: Jev LangChain and other framework integrations (TypeSafe AI). Of 6 Jev framework packages read in source, 4 are pre-1.0 and none comes from TypeSafe; 4 raise Jev errors to your code, while the community Spring AI filter passes passages through unscreened.

New section on Where to use: Jev is not listed in the Amazon Bedrock model catalog or the Azure AI Foundry model catalog (checked 5 Oct 2026, 05:18–05:19 UTC), and TypeSafe's docs do not mention either. Call TypeSafe's API or a gateway.

When Jev fails updated: of 51 Jev implementations in 9 use cases read in source, 30 stop or hold the action when Jev errors and 6 let it through unchecked: 4 content-moderation bots, one Claude Code hook and one Spring AI passage filter. Adds 8 browser and 4 framework rows and a copyable checklist.

Products refreshed: 72 rows (A 55, B 16, C 1); Jev for Chrome, computer-use-jev and jev-android upgraded from B to A; 5 new grade-A browser rows; six framework packages listed as not counted. 0 independently verified in production.

Small additions: Strands Decider 2B on Alternatives (benchmark and AWS attribution Reported), a Zapier note on the n8n page, an EU-hosting line on data privacy, and tool-documentation links on Jev as a judge. Rate-limit check dates moved to 5 Oct.

Corrections: langchain-typesafe 0.0.1a3 was uploaded on 20 Sep 2026, not 4 Oct; @effect/ai-typesafe is 4.0.1; the Spring AI integration is a community package; the AndroidWorld paper (arXiv 2609.30186) was submitted on 24 Sep. The Python page notes that the Pydantic AI Gateway did not list TypeSafe on 5 Oct.

Access status rechecked 5 Oct 2026, 05:13 UTC: unchanged (signups open, no new-user credit, API operational). Price, limits and the subprocessor list unchanged; the API's 90-day uptime moved from 99.826% to 99.829%. Check dates updated on Home, access status and the cost worksheet.

New page: Jev trading bot and fraud gates (TypeSafe AI). Of 4 Jev trading bots read in source, 2 can still place a new order when Jev errors; all 4 can trade without Jev. None of 3 fraud or payment gates moves money. In two bots "mock" means no Jev, not no trading. No advice and no performance figures.

New page: When Jev fails (TypeSafe AI). Of 39 Jev implementations read in source, 21 stop or hold the action when Jev errors and 5 let it through unchecked: 4 content-moderation bots and one Claude Code hook. Counts per condition and use case with "not recorded" counts, and an 8-question checklist.

New page: Jev as a judge (TypeSafe AI). Of 4 Jev judge tools read in source, DeepEval stops the run on a Jev error; the other 3 drop the item from the score, and openlayer jevals still reports it as passed. Judge studies B02, B06 and B08 copied unchanged.

Products refreshed: 67 rows (A 47, B 19, C 1); jev-trader and Jev Trade upgraded from B to A; 6 new grade-A rows; QuantDinger re-pinned at a5a9f4c; DeepEval JevEval and openlayer jevals listed as library features, not counted. 0 independently verified in production.

Home notice: TypeSafe's trust center added Nebius and CoreWeave as subprocessors on 2 Oct (6 listed; prompts "processed, but not stored" in TypeSafe's wording; SOC 2 report not seen). Shown at rank 4; the WorkflowEvals notice stays current but is no longer shown. Details on data privacy.

Correction on email and lead sorting: unsure cells relabelled under the 4 Oct terms (Jevmail acts-anyway, flagged; spam-leadgen fallback: not qualified; vynnlee held: Review label), and the cost range now starts at about $0.025 per 1,000 very short emails instead of $0.004.

Correction: QuantDinger links on the Use cases hub, testing without a key and Products now point to commit a5a9f4c; the 28 Sep line links had gone stale after the file was rewritten. Behaviour unchanged.
Claude Code and MCP: oh-my-claudecode is described as advisory at default settings; v5.6.1 (3 Oct) noted as a patch, failure path checked at v5.6.0.

Access status rechecked 4 Oct 2026, 05:15 UTC: unchanged (signups open, no new-user credit, API operational). Price, limits and route listings unchanged; check dates updated on Home, access status, Where to use, errors and rate limits, limitations and the cost worksheet.

New page: Jev email classifier (TypeSafe AI). Of 5 email and lead sorters read in source, none touches the mailbox when Jev errors; of the 3 that can write to Gmail or IMAP, only 1 routes unsure mail to a Review label. Project table in the shared failure terms, cost per 1,000 emails (pool arithmetic beside the Reported demo figure), seven design rules, data and permissions box.

New page: Jev n8n node (TypeSafe AI). Only the scoped @typesafe-ai/n8n-nodes-typesafe-ai is TypeSafe's (npm provenance, n8n-verified); the unscoped n8n-nodes-typesafe-ai is a third party's. All 5 nodes read stop the workflow on a Jev error by default; Continue On Fail behaviour compared.

Products hub refreshed: 61 ledger rows (A 39, B 21, C 1); 24 new grade-A rows from the triage, routing, moderation, email and n8n audits; 0 independently verified in production. 5 of 7 published claims rechecked and unchanged; the 2 VentureBeat-relayed claims were not rechecked. LiteLLM listed under not counted as products.
